rv.q: But, in the space of three hours, it gives us an effective summation of the story and captures both the pain and the pity of a war that almost defies comprehension.
Sebastian Faulks ’ wonderful 1993 novel Birdsong is a love story, a chronicle of horrendous conditions in the trenches of the First World War, and a tale of amazing human courage and resilience.
But also, to one’s surprise, it also seems slightly plodding, arch and strangely one-dimensional.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this WWI adaptation: some praise its ingenious staging and successful distillation of Faulks's novel, while others find the transition from page to stage problematic.
